contentObjective: I can use patterns and relationships to make sense of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle and think logically about its solutions.
languageObjective: I can describe a puzzle strategy using the words pattern, rule, and predict.

steps: 1. Deconstruct complex multi-step problems into smaller, repeatable sub-tasks
2. Trace patterns from simple cases to formulate general mathematical rules
3. Verify algorithmic rules across edge cases and increasing problem sizes

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The 15 Puzzle
revealWordProblem.text:
The 15 Puzzle is a sliding puzzle with 15 numbered tiles in a frame 4 tiles high and 4 tiles wide. The goal is to arrange the tiles in order from 1 to 15 by sliding one tile at a time into the open space. Some starting arrangements can be solved and some cannot.
Question: Try solving the 15 Puzzle shown. Then make an argument for whether it is solvable or unsolvable.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A 4 by 4 sliding puzzle holding tiles numbered 1 to 15 with one empty space.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: I read the tiles in order, row by row, and counted how many pairs are out of order. A sideways slide never changes that count, and an up-or-down slide changes it in a way I can track along with the row the empty space is in. So I compared my starting count with what the finished puzzle needs, and used that comparison — not guessing and sliding — as the argument for whether this arrangement can reach 1 through 15 in order.

questions.stem: What is the fewest number of moves needed to solve a three-disc Tower of Hanoi puzzle?
questions.explanation: It takes at least 7 moves to solve a three-disc Tower of Hanoi puzzle.
choiceFeedback: 3 is the number of DISCS — moving each disc only once is impossible because of the size rule.
6 doubles the 3 discs but forgets the extra move — the pattern is double and add 1, so 3 discs need 7.
9 is 3 × 3, but the fewest-moves count follows the doubling pattern, not disc × disc.
hints: It is more than one move per disc.
A two-disc tower already takes 3 moves.
Double 3 and add 1.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el menor número de movimientos necesarios para resolver la Torre de Hanói de tres discos?
questions.explanationEs: Se necesitan al menos 7 movimientos para resolver la Torre de Hanói de tres discos.
hintsEs: Es más de un movimiento por disco.
Una torre de dos discos ya toma 3 movimientos.
Duplica 3 y suma 1.

questions.stem: Which move is against the rules of the Tower of Hanoi?
choices: Moving one disc at a time
Moving the top disc from a stack
Placing a larger disc on top of a smaller disc
Placing a smaller disc on top of a larger disc
questions.explanation: A larger disc can never be on top of a smaller disc — that is the rule that makes the puzzle a puzzle.
choiceFeedback: One disc at a time is exactly what the rules require, not what they forbid.
You may only move the TOP disc of a stack — that move follows the rules.
Smaller on top of larger is the legal direction; it is the reverse that is banned.
hints: Two of these are the rules themselves.
Think about disc SIZES.
Which stacking order would crush a smaller disc?
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál movimiento va contra las reglas de la Torre de Hanói?
questions.explanationEs: Un disco más grande nunca puede estar sobre uno más pequeño — esa es la regla que hace que el rompecabezas sea un rompecabezas.
hintsEs: Dos de estas son las reglas mismas.
Piensa en los TAMAÑOS de los discos.
¿Cuál orden de apilado aplastaría un disco más pequeño?

questions.stem: What will the solved puzzle look like?
choices: The discs in the same order — smallest on top to largest on bottom — but on a different rod
The discs in reverse order, largest on top
The discs spread out with one disc on each rod
The discs back on the starting rod in any order
questions.explanation: The goal is to rebuild the whole stack, smallest to largest, on a different rod.
choiceFeedback: Largest on top would break the rule — a larger disc can never sit on a smaller one.
Spreading the discs out is a middle step, not the finished puzzle.
The stack must END on a different rod, and the size order is required, not optional.
hints: Imagine the ending before you start.
The stack looks just like the start.
Only its rod has changed.
questions.explanationEs: La meta es reconstruir toda la pila, del más pequeño al más grande, en otra varilla.
hintsEs: Imagina el final antes de empezar.
La pila se ve igual que al inicio.
Solo cambió su varilla.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: Doubling the previous number of steps but forgetting to add 1 — answering 14 instead of 15 for four discs, or 30 instead of 31 for five.

level1.stem: Use the rule “double, then add 1.” A 2-disc tower takes 3 moves. How many moves does a 3-disc tower take?
level1.stemEs: Usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1». Una torre de 2 discos toma 3 movimientos. ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de 3 discos?
hints: Double 3. Then add 1.
hintsEs: Duplica 3. Luego suma 1.

level1.stem: Towers of 3 and 4 discs take 7 and 15 moves. How many moves does a 5-disc tower take?
level1.stemEs: Las torres de 3 y 4 discos toman 7 y 15 movimientos. ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de 5 discos?
hints: Find the rule from 7 to 15. Use it on 15.
hintsEs: Halla la regla de 7 a 15. Úsala con 15.
level1.explanation: Find the rule from 7 to 15: 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 Use the rule on 15: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31
level1.explanationEs: Halla la regla de 7 a 15: 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 Usa la regla con 15: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31

level1.stem: A pattern uses the rule “double, then add 1.” It starts 3, 7. What number comes next?
level1.stemEs: Un patrón usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1». Empieza 3, 7. ¿Qué número sigue?
hints: Use the rule on 7.
hintsEs: Usa la regla con 7.

level1.stem: A pattern starts at 4. The rule is “double, then add 1.” What is the 3rd number in the pattern?
level1.stemEs: Un patrón empieza en 4. La regla es «duplica y luego suma 1». ¿Cuál es el 3.er número del patrón?
hints: Use the rule on 4 to get the 2nd number. Then use the rule again.
hintsEs: Usa la regla con 4 para obtener el 2.º número. Luego usa la regla otra vez.
level1.explanation: Use the rule on 4: 4 × 2 + 1 = 9 Use the rule on 9: 9 × 2 + 1 = 19
level1.explanationEs: Usa la regla con 4: 4 × 2 + 1 = 9 Usa la regla con 9: 9 × 2 + 1 = 19

level1.stem: A 6-disc tower takes 63 moves. How many moves does a 7-disc tower take?
level1.stemEs: Una torre de 6 discos toma 63 movimientos. ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de 7 discos?
hints: Use the rule “double, then add 1” on 63.
hintsEs: Usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1» con 63.

level2.stem: A 4-disc tower takes 15 moves. Sam says a 5-disc tower takes 16 moves, because it has 1 more disc. Is he right? How many moves does it take?
level2.stemEs: Una torre de 4 discos toma 15 movimientos. Sam dice que una torre de 5 discos toma 16 movimientos, porque tiene 1 disco más. ¿Tiene razón? ¿Cuántos movimientos toma?
hints: Sam only added 1 move. The rule says to double first.
hintsEs: Sam solo sumó 1 movimiento. La regla dice que primero hay que duplicar.

level2.stem: A 10-disc tower takes 1,023 moves. How many moves does an 11-disc tower take?
level2.stemEs: Una torre de 10 discos toma 1,023 movimientos. ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de 11 discos?
hints: Use the rule “double, then add 1.”
hintsEs: Usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1».

level2.stem: An 8-disc tower takes 255 moves. How many moves does a 9-disc tower take?
level2.stemEs: Una torre de 8 discos toma 255 movimientos. ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de 9 discos?
hints: Use the pattern rule on 255.
hintsEs: Usa la regla del patrón con 255.

level2.stem: A pattern uses the rule “double, then add 1.” The 4th number is 95. What is the 1st number?
level2.stemEs: Un patrón usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1». El 4.º número es 95. ¿Cuál es el 1.er número?
hints: Undo the rule three times: subtract 1, then halve.
hintsEs: Deshaz la regla tres veces: resta 1 y luego divide entre 2.
level2.explanation: Undo the rule from 95: (95 − 1) ÷ 2 = 47 Undo it two more times: (47 − 1) ÷ 2 = 23; (23 − 1) ÷ 2 = 11
level2.explanationEs: Deshaz la regla desde 95: (95 − 1) ÷ 2 = 47 Deshazla dos veces más: (47 − 1) ÷ 2 = 23; (23 − 1) ÷ 2 = 11

level2.stem: Toothpicks make a row of squares. 1 square uses 4 toothpicks. 2 squares use 7. 3 squares use 10. How many toothpicks do 6 squares use?
level2.stemEs: Unos palillos forman una fila de cuadrados. 1 cuadrado usa 4 palillos. 2 cuadrados usan 7. 3 cuadrados usan 10. ¿Cuántos palillos usan 6 cuadrados?
hints: Look from each row to the next. What do you add each time?
hintsEs: Mira de cada fila a la siguiente. ¿Qué sumas cada vez?
level2.explanation: Find the rule from row to row: 4 + 3 = 7; 7 + 3 = 10 Keep adding 3 to reach 6 squares: 10 → 13 → 16 → 19
level2.explanationEs: Halla la regla de una fila a otra: 4 + 3 = 7; 7 + 3 = 10 Sigue sumando 3 hasta llegar a 6 cuadrados: 10 → 13 → 16 → 19

buildFigure.caption: Look from each row to the next row.
buildFigure.captionEs: Mira de cada fila a la fila siguiente.

level3.stem: A 3-disc tower takes 7 moves. Jay says a 6-disc tower takes 7 × 2 = 14 moves, because 6 is double 3. How many moves does a 6-disc tower take?
level3.stemEs: Una torre de 3 discos toma 7 movimientos. Jay dice que una torre de 6 discos toma 7 × 2 = 14 movimientos, porque 6 es el doble de 3. ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de 6 discos?
hints: The rule goes from one disc to the next disc. Use it once for each new disc.
hintsEs: La regla va de un disco al disco siguiente. Úsala una vez por cada disco nuevo.
level3.explanation: Use the rule for 4 discs: 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 Use it for 5 discs and 6 discs: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31; 31 × 2 + 1 = 63
level3.explanationEs: Usa la regla para 4 discos: 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 Úsala para 5 discos y 6 discos: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31; 31 × 2 + 1 = 63

level3.stem: A pattern uses the rule “double, then add 1.” The 4th number is 79. What is the 1st number?
level3.stemEs: Un patrón usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1». El 4.º número es 79. ¿Cuál es el 1.er número?
hints: Work backward: subtract 1, then halve. Do it three times.
hintsEs: Trabaja hacia atrás: resta 1 y luego divide entre 2. Hazlo tres veces.
level3.explanation: Undo the rule from 79: (79 − 1) ÷ 2 = 39 Undo it two more times: (39 − 1) ÷ 2 = 19; (19 − 1) ÷ 2 = 9
level3.explanationEs: Deshaz la regla desde 79: (79 − 1) ÷ 2 = 39 Deshazla dos veces más: (39 − 1) ÷ 2 = 19; (19 − 1) ÷ 2 = 9

level3.stem: Each week, Maya doubles her savings and then adds $3. After 3 weeks, she has $53. How much money did she start with?
level3.stemEs: Cada semana, Maya duplica sus ahorros y luego suma $3. Después de 3 semanas, tiene $53. ¿Con cuánto dinero empezó?
hints: Work backward. Undo “add $3” first, then undo “double.”
hintsEs: Trabaja hacia atrás. Primero deshaz «suma $3» y luego deshaz «duplica».
level3.explanationEs: Deshaz la semana 3: (53 − 3) ÷ 2 = 25 Deshaz la semana 2 y luego la semana 1: (25 − 3) ÷ 2 = 11; (11 − 3) ÷ 2 = 4

level3.stem: Use the rule “double, then add 1.” A 10-disc tower takes 1,023 moves. What is the smallest tower that takes more than 5,000 moves?
level3.stemEs: Usa la regla «duplica y luego suma 1». Una torre de 10 discos toma 1,023 movimientos. ¿Cuál es la torre más pequeña que toma más de 5,000 movimientos?
hints: Keep using the rule. Stop at the first number of moves greater than 5,000.
hintsEs: Sigue usando la regla. Detente en el primer número de movimientos mayor que 5,000.
level3.explanation: Use the rule for 11 and 12 discs: 1023 × 2 + 1 = 2047; 2047 × 2 + 1 = 4095 Use the rule for 13 discs: 4095 × 2 + 1 = 8191 Compare with 5,000: 4095 < 5000 < 8191
level3.explanationEs: Usa la regla para 11 y 12 discos: 1023 × 2 + 1 = 2047; 2047 × 2 + 1 = 4095 Usa la regla para 13 discos: 4095 × 2 + 1 = 8191 Compara con 5,000: 4095 < 5000 < 8191

level3.stem: A five-disc tower takes 31 steps. Using the pattern rule, how many steps would a SIX-disc tower take?
level3.explanation: Apply the rule to 31: double it and add 1, so 31 × 2 + 1 = 63 steps.
choiceFeedback: 32 adds 1 to 31 but forgets to double first.
36 adds 5 to 31 — the rule doubles the steps rather than adding the disc count.
62 doubles the 31 steps but forgets to add 1.
hints: The rule works from any row of the table.
Double, then add 1.
level3.stemEs: Una torre de cinco discos toma 31 pasos. Usando la regla del patrón, ¿cuántos pasos tomaría una torre de SEIS discos?
level3.explanationEs: Aplica la regla a 31: duplícalo y suma 1, así que 31 × 2 + 1 = 63 pasos.
hintsEs: La regla funciona desde cualquier fila de la tabla.
Duplica y luego suma 1.

tool.title: Fewest Moves in Tower of Hanoi
tool.caption: Each bar doubles the one before it and adds 1: 1, 3, 7, 15, 31. One more disc nearly doubles the work, so the bars grow far faster than the disc count.
